top_skus: Refined palmolein 850 g / 1 L pouch — GENUINELY ABSENT (probe verified). ARY's cheapest working cooking oil is Fortune Soya 750 Ml at ₹202/L and Mashal 500 Ml at ₹201/L; palmolein lands ~₹150-165/L. This is the one real price-point hole in the category. Retail half is my weakest number (palmolein is a canteen frying oil, not a North-Indian household oil); the institutional half rests on Hunger Heroes' proven appetite for cheap bulk oil.

Sealed 15 kg / 15 L institutional refined-soya tin — GENUINELY ABSENT in soya (only two 15 L SKUs exist store-wide, both zero-sale). Adds ₹0 revenue: Hunger Heroes already buys 1,890 × 1 L Fortune Soya pouches (₹2.60 L) + 1,280 L decanted loose soya (₹1.79 L). The prize is cost per litre and getting off the decanting counter, not a new sale.

Refined soyabean 5 L jar — NOT an add, a REORDER. Jivo Soyabean Oil 5 Ltr (0D4R) is already listed and active; 24 units bought ever, last purchase 2024-03, zero on hand, zero sales. It has never been stocked. Buying it is inventory, not assortment.

DO NOT ADD — branded ghee in any pack (1 L, 500 ml, 200 ml, sachet, 5 L tin). All 11 branded ghee SKUs sold ₹0 in 12 months except Mahaan 200 Ml (2 pcs, ₹294, Sep-2025). Each was bought once (1-15 units), sold through, never reordered. Meanwhile Loose Desi Ghee did ₹14.00 L at ₹997/L — residents pay a ~50% per-litre premium over branded Amul/Verka and still choose loose. That is a taste preference, not a gap.

DO NOT ADD — ghee sachets / 200-500 ml small packs. The loose counter already dispenses exactly these sizes: of 866 loose-ghee lines, 31 were under 150 ml, 108 at 150-300 ml and 230 at 300-600 ml — 43% of all lines are sub-600 ml. The 'small-pack hole' the demand research flagged does not exist.

DO NOT ADD — flaxseed oil, cold-pressed/chekku sesame, avocado/walnut oil, cooking-oil spray, bakery shortening, A2/Gir/bilona ghee, organic ghee, sunflower 5 L/15 kg, mustard 15 L tin, vanaspati 15 kg tin. All genuinely absent (probe verified) and all long tail. Live velocity benchmark for a premium oil facing on this campus: Jivo Sesame Oil 1 Ltr @₹450 sold 5 units in 12 months; Jivo EV Olive 5 Ltr sold 1; Minchy's Kernel Cold Pressed 200 Ml sold 1. Cold-pressed shelf life is 3-6 months — these expire before they sell.

THE ACTUAL MONEY, and it is not assortment: 6 of the top 12 SKUs by revenue (₹22.3 L = 73% of the category) sit at zero or under 5 days of cover TODAY — Loose Desi Ghee 16 L (4.2 d), Fortune Soya 1 Ltr 17 pcs (3.1 d), Soyabean Fortune_L ZERO, Desi Ghee 1 Ltr ZERO, Fortune Soya 750 Ml ZERO, Jivo Mustard 1 Ltr Pouch ZERO (last sale 2026-04-08). Meanwhile Jivo Cold Pressed Kachi Ghani Pouch carries 319 days, Jivo Canola 1 L Pouch 240 days, Jivo EV Olive 1 L 231 days.

SECOND ACTUAL MONEY ITEM: two SKUs sell below cost. Desi Ghee 1 Ltr (0ETN) cost ₹471.18 vs ₹439.43 net sale = −₹9,867/yr (confirmed independently by `ary assort leak`). Jivo Extra Virgin Olive Oil 1 Ltr (0B20) cost ₹670.48 vs ~₹631 net = ~−₹2,650/yr (PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed — the leak tool did not flag it). Fixing two price tags returns ~₹12,500/yr for zero capital — about a third of the entire assortment prize.
penetration_assumption: Three separate assumptions, stated before the numbers. (1) PALMOLEIN, Rs 2.22 L/yr: of ~250 resident staff families (vault-VERIFIED as "more than 200 families"; the exact count is the softest input in this analysis), 12% = 30 families buy one 850 g palmolein pouch a month at Rs 150 (= Rs 54,000/yr), and Hunger Heroes takes 100 L/month at Rs 140/L for frying (= Rs 1.68 L/yr). (2) LONG TAIL, Rs 36,000/yr: the nine remaining genuinely-absent lines (flaxseed, chekku sesame, avocado/walnut, oil spray, bakery shortening, A2/organic ghee, sunflower 5 L, mustard tin, vanaspati tin) each do what the nearest comparable premium SKU already in the store does — Jivo Sesame Oil 1 Ltr sold 5 units in 12 months, Jivo EV Olive 5 Ltr sold 1 — so 9 lines x ~Rs 4,000 each. (3) INSTITUTIONAL TIN, Rs 0 revenue / Rs 19,700 margin: ARY converts the ~3,170 L/yr of institutional soya it ALREADY sells from 1 L pouches to sealed 15 kg tins at a 5% trade discount on the VERIFIED pouch landed cost of Rs 124.54/L. Range at 4-6% is Rs 15,800-23,700. That discount is a trade assumption, not an ARY price — ARY has never bought a soya tin, and the one tin it does buy (Jivo Canola 15 L at Rs 2,500 = Rs 166.67/L) is DEARER per litre than the 1 L soya pouch, which argues against assuming tins are always cheaper. Total: Rs 2.58 L incremental revenue, Rs 41,100 incremental gross margin. Margin rates applied are the category's own realised rates, not a blanket percentage: 7.2% blended for the palmolein mix (institutional lines run 5-9%), 15% for premium tail (Jivo Olive Extra Light runs 18.95%, Jivo Soyabean 1 Ltr 19.5%).
probe_evidence: Every "missing" verdict in the coverage diff was re-tested with `ary assort probe` before I accepted it, on the live window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31 (feed VERIFIED live: last sale 2026-08-30 20:57). CONFIRMED ABSENT: `probe palmolein palm ruchi rajni` -> 4 SKUs, all Palmolive shower gel and Hari Darshan Rajnigandha agarbatti, zero oils, so no palmolein exists in any pack. `probe "oil spray" "cooking spray"` -> 0 SKUs matched. `probe shortening margarine bakery vanaspati` -> 13 SKUs, all La Bakery biscuits and Gagan/Rath vanaspati retail packs, no bakery fat. `probe flaxseed flax alsi linseed` -> 5 SKUs, all whole seed plus one Cipla Omnigel pain rub, no flaxseed oil. `probe bilona a2 gir "cow ghee" organic` -> 151 SKUs living in Night Wear, Winter Wear, Womens Wear, Tea and Footwear, not one a ghee. Direct SQL for avocado/walnut+oil -> 3 SKUs, all Marico Hair & Care hair oil. Full-catalogue large-pack sweep (%15 Ltr%/%15 Kg%/%Tin%/%5 Ltr%/%Jar%) -> the largest edible-oil pack that SELLS anywhere in ARY is 5 L; the only two 15 L SKUs (Ambuja 0013, Jivo Canola 00AL) have zero retail sales. PROBE OVERTURNED THE DIFF IN THREE PLACES: (a) `probe sunflower sunlite sundrop` returned 21 SKUs and showed Jivo Cold Press Sunflower Oil 1 Ltr live at Rs 18,020 / 106 units, last sale 2026-08-29 — sunflower is covered at 1 L, only the 5 L/tin is absent; (b) `probe sesame til chekku gingelly "cold press"` found Pansari Til Oil 500 Ml (Rs 25,320) and 200 Ml (Rs 15,425) selling, so sesame is covered — only the premium chekku grade is absent, and the live velocity of the nearest premium comparable is 5 units/year; (c) `probe ghee` showed Loose Desi Ghee at Rs 14,00,506 across 1,405 L with a quantity distribution that already covers 150-600 ml, killing the diff's "small-pack ghee is the real hole" conclusion outright. THE DIFF'S FRAMING WAS ALSO WRONG ON THE DENOMINATOR: it sized the category at "3.4% of ARY vs 8-10% normal", but ARY's Rs 7.67 Cr gross includes Rs 1.83 Cr of Garments, Rs 65 L of Toiletries and Rs 66 L of prepared Menu Items. Against the food basket (Grocery + Confectionery + Fruits&Veg + Drinks + Frozen = Rs 3.45 Cr) oils is 8.8%, inside the normal band; against the Grocery department alone (Rs 1.35 Cr) it is 22.5% and the single largest group. There is no category-level shortfall.
kill_reason: Not a FALSE_GAP — two lines are genuinely absent and worth adding — but the gap is an order of magnitude smaller than the research fleet implied, and the category's real problem is replenishment. THE EVIDENCE FOR AVAILABILITY, all VERIFIED on the live window: (1) Six of the top twelve SKUs by revenue, Rs 22.3 L = 73% of the category, are at zero or under five days of stock cover right now, while the parent's slow-moving Jivo lines carry 231-319 days. (2) Measured stock-out loss on gaps of 7+ days for SKUs that normally sell every 1-3 days: Rs 2,81,578 of sales in 12 months (Jivo Mustard 1 Ltr Rs 62,155 across 107 lost days and an 85-day gap; Jivo Soyabean 1 Ltr Pouch Rs 46,346; Mashal Mustard 500 Ml Rs 42,983; Loose Desi Ghee Rs 40,618) — that is 10x the entire assortment prize and needs no new SKU. (3) Of 79 dormant SKUs, 42 have NEVER been purchased once in the system's history and only 3 hold any stock today (127.82 units, of which 65.81 are the canteen's canola tins). The dead 62% of the shelf is stale master data, not shelf space or capital — delisting releases Rs 0, and "add this SKU" is meaningless when the SKU was already listed and never bought. (4) The national-brand wall the diff called dead (Fortune Kachi Ghani, Dhara Soyabean, Patanjali Mustard, Saffola Gold x2, Fortune Sunlite, Fortune Rice Bran) was never stocked, not rejected: purchase-ever = 0 on every one. That is an availability failure dressed as an assortment one. (5) The category's realised gross margin is 3.66% — Rs 1,00,172 of gross margin on Rs 27.38 L of net sales, costed off PurchaseDetail (pre-tax cost) against SaleDetail net of GST for the 42 SKUs that both sold and were bought in the window, 97.5% of category sales. At that rate a Rs 10 L revenue "opportunity" here is worth Rs 37,000. Any recommendation sized on revenue rather than margin is off by ~27x. (6) The institutional-tin "gap" is not a revenue gap at all: Hunger Heroes and Akal Academy already bought Rs 6.98 L of oils and ghee in 12 months, in the wrong format — 1,890 one-litre pouches and 1,280 L decanted by hand. The sale is booked; only the cost and the legality are wrong.
blockers: LEGAL, and it is the biggest thing in this category: 2,678 L are sold BY THE LITRE from a decanting counter — Loose Desi Ghee 1,397.8 L (Rs 14.00 L) and Soyabean Fortune_L 1,280 L (Rs 1.79 L) — which is Rs 15.73 L, 51.7% of the whole category. FSSAI requires sealed packs of 15 kg or less for edible oil and state FDAs were prosecuting loose edible-oil sale in Aug 2026. Loose Desi Ghee's own tax records are inconsistent too (141 lines at 0% tax, 725 at 7.38%). Any move to grow bulk or institutional volume must go through sealed tins, never the decanting counter. VERIFIED volumes; the regulation itself is NOT-CHECKED by me, it is carried from the demand research.

REPLENISHMENT, not capital or shelf, is the binding constraint. The dead tail holds zero stock so there is no cash to release and no facing to free. The buyer is letting Rs 22 L of proven sellers run to zero while the parent's slow lines sit on 4-10 months of cover. Adding SKUs to a store that cannot keep its top six in stock makes the problem worse, not better.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP. ARY's oil supply is dominated by the parent, Jivo Wellness (intercompany), plus Dharam Pal & Sons for loose soya. A palmolein pouch or a sealed 15 kg tin needs a distributor willing to serve a ghat road 30-50 km from town for ~Rs 2 L/yr of offtake. NOT-CHECKED: I did not search the supplier master for a candidate, and this could kill the palmolein line on its own.

SHELF LIFE. Cold-pressed oils run 3-6 months. At this campus's demonstrated premium-oil velocity — Jivo Sesame Oil 1 Ltr sold 5 units in 12 months, Jivo EV Olive 5 Ltr sold 1 — a cold-pressed sesame or flaxseed facing expires before it sells. This is why I sized the long tail at Rs 4,000 a line, not Rs 40,000.

A SHRINKING POPULATION. Vault-VERIFIED: Eternal University enrolment 1,102, flat across ten years; Akal Academy board cohorts down 22% to 50%; the permanent off-vacation resident base measures 1,700-2,300 against a term-time 4,550-4,800. And most residents are hostel students eating at the mess, not households cooking at home — the honest denominator for retail cooking oil is ~200-300 staff families, not 4,700 residents. Any range plan assuming a growing customer base is planning against a decline.

LICENCE AND COLD CHAIN ARE NOT BLOCKERS HERE. Edible oil and ghee need no cold chain, and ARY already operates under an FSSAI registration (it is selling loose ghee under it today). NOT-CHECKED: I did not read the licence itself or confirm its scope covers repacking.
CAPITAL is trivial: two new lines at Rs 2.58 L of annual revenue need roughly Rs 25,000-40,000 of working stock. Capital is not what is stopping this.
